state: BREACH-DOCTOR-1 runs in qnfo-fleet-control (breachDoctorTick, called from the */10 slot of scheduledOnce, on main since 0.52.0). The second path qnfo-cloud-ops 1.39.0 jobBreachDoctorWatch only DETECTS and REPORTS (it writes doctor_tick_age_min and files one deduped 'BREACH-DOCTOR-1: doctor stalled (watch)' issue); when the doctor tick stalls nothing ACTS. agent_issues 1000397 stays open for the acting half; its D1 contract (class issue-1000397) passes only when control_registry 'breach-doctor-switch' has alternate_tested_at and capability_ledger has a 'breach-doctor:second-path-playbooks' row. Read the issue text (agent_issues 1000397), docs/breach-doctor/ENGINE-DESIGN.md and docs/breach-doctor/LOOP-MAP.md. Failure class the second path must cover: the fleet-control scheduled slot is starved or crashes before the doctor runs (the 04:42Z-06:12Z SQLITE_NOMEM heartbeat outage of 2026-10-26 is the observed case), not a dead D1.
evidence: The engine is one block '// ---- BREACH-DOCTOR-1:BEGIN/END ----' in qnfo-fleet-control/worker.js; the same validators (bdValidateRule, bdWriteWhy, bdReadOnlyWhy) guard every playbook statement. Duplicating them into qnfo-cloud-ops would give two validators that drift (the validator was patched three times in one day: 0.53.0, 0.53.1, 0.53.2), so the second path must RUN the engine, not copy it. A Worker's fetch to a workers.dev host of its own account fails (issue-1190 artifact), so the call has to be a service binding. CLAUDE.md '#1703 Internal calls': internal workers authenticate to each other by service-binding props (props = { caller = '<worker name>' } under the [[services]] binding in wrangler.toml; the canonical deploy installs it, qnfo-ops BINDING-PROPS-APPLY-1). Find an existing fetch handler that checks ctx.props.caller (grep 'props.caller' across */worker.js; qnfo-email and qnfo-ai are the references) and copy its shape. qnfo-cloud-ops/wrangler.toml has [[services]] blocks for EMAIL, RESEARCH_EXEC, QNFO_INFRA, QNFO_AI to copy. Check the fleet graph (GET https://qnfo-memory-mcp.q08.workers.dev/fleet-graph/impact?id=worker:qnfo-fleet-control) before adding the binding. Concurrency: the engine takes a per-case lease (lease_until) and records tick_id; verify by reading breachDoctorTick that two overlapping ticks (the cron one and the watch one) cannot act on the same case twice, and write the test that proves it.

lever.change: (1) qnfo-fleet-control/worker.js: add POST /breach-doctor/run (path inside the existing fetch router; MINOR version bump: a route and a decision the worker now takes for another worker) that accepts only a service-binding caller whose ctx.props.caller is 'qnfo-cloud-ops' (a request without it gets 403 and writes nothing), refuses while ops_config breach_doctor is 'off', runs breachDoctorTick(env, ...) once in this invocation (its own isolate, so a starved */10 slot does not starve it) and returns {ok, tick_id, cases, acted, verified, tick_age_min_before} without any issue text. The tick it runs records breach_diagnosis_events rows exactly as a cron tick does plus detail source=watch. (2) qnfo-cloud-ops/wrangler.toml: [[services]] binding = 'FLEET_CONTROL', service = 'qnfo-fleet-control', props = { caller = 'qnfo-cloud-ops' }. (3) qnfo-cloud-ops/worker.js jobBreachDoctorWatch (MINOR bump): when doctor_tick_age_min > 30 and ops_config breach_doctor is not 'off', call env.FLEET_CONTROL.fetch('https://internal/breach-doctor/run', {method:'POST'}) at most once per 30 minutes (dedupe on the newest cloud_ops_events kind breach-doctor-watch row with detail acted=1), write the answer (ok, acted, verified, error code) into the cloud_ops_events row of that run, and keep filing the existing stall issue. A missing binding (env.FLEET_CONTROL undefined, a deploy that landed before the binding) is reported as a skipped run with reason no-binding, never a throw. (4) A daily DRILL in the same job: once per 24 hours even when the doctor is healthy, call the route once and require that a new breach_diagnosis_events tick row with source=watch appears; on success stamp control_registry 'breach-doctor-switch' alternate_tested_at and spof_registry alternate_tested_at for the doctor tick row (honest: the alternate actually ran) and record last_exercised_at on the capability_ledger row. (5) migration migrations/2026-10-26-breach-doctor-watch-acting.sql (APPLY-BY ci, DB qnfo-audit, one-line Rollback, decision_log row): capability_ledger row 'breach-doctor:second-path-playbooks' (provenance, prerequisites, reliability 'unmeasured until the first drill'), control_registry breach-doctor-switch alternate_path text corrected to name the acting half, issue 1000397 description paragraph saying what was delivered; the migration must NOT stamp any alternate_tested_at (the drill does). (6) tests: fleet-control route test (403 without props, 403 with another caller, refuses when off, runs one tick, concurrent-lease test proving no double action), cloud-ops job test (stale to call, fresh to no call except the daily drill, no-binding skip, error recorded, stamp only after a real new tick row), migration test; they must fail on the pre-change code.
lever.preference: Keep the cloud-ops side small. Do not copy any validator into qnfo-cloud-ops.
